picks.source: I amsterdam · Your Little Black Book · Sunday Market

picks.title: Parea
picks.blurb: Greek stick bar with wood-fired flatbreads and grilled souvlaki, fresh from Angelo Kremmydas (Gitane, Massalia).
picks.source: Your Little Black Book · I amsterdam

picks.title: Rommelmarkt bij QRU
picks.blurb: Flea Market at QRU – Final Edition of 2026 On Sunday 22 November, QRU in Amsterdam East hosts its final flea market of 2026.
picks.source: I amsterdam · Your Little Black Book

picks.title: Party on Sunday: Sinterklaas at the World Museum Amsterdam (6+)

picks.title: Sinterklaas weekend at Pathé: movies, Pieten, and putting out shoes
picks.blurb: On Saturday, November 21 and Sunday, November 22, Pathé is organizing a special Sinterklaas weekend.

picks.title: Play, Share, Swap & Recycle Festival: swap toys and children's clothing in De Hallen
picks.blurb: With Sinterklaas and the holidays approaching, this is a great tip for families! On Saturday, November 21 and Sunday, November 22, De Passage in De Hallen will…

picks.blurb: On Sunday, November 22, Poppentheater Koos Kneus in Amsterdam-East is presenting the Sinterklaas performance *Er staat een paard in de tuin!* (There’s a horse…

picks.title: Marcos Kueh – PRESENT
picks.blurb: Four woven tapestries exploring father-child bonds in historic bedroom; artist talk December 12 about personal narratives.

picks.title: Sinterklaas at 't Blauwe Theehuis: put out your shoe and meet the Saint
picks.blurb: There are also fun Sinterklaas activities for children at 't Blauwe Theehuis in the Vondelpark in the coming weeks!

picks.title: Enoteca Capri
picks.blurb: A good glass of Italian wine, crisp spuntini and creamy pasta: at Enoteca Capri on the Lindengracht, you’ll briefly feel as though you’re in Italy.
picks.source: I amsterdam · Your Little Black Book

picks.title: Museum Market
picks.blurb: Every month, you will find the Museum Market on Museumplein. A market featuring art, illustrations, jewelry, ceramics, fashion, design, and delicacies from…
picks.source: I amsterdam · Your Little Black Book

picks.title: The Maker Market
picks.blurb: New editions, discover new creators! The Maker Market takes place monthly at De Hallen in Amsterdam-West, a vibrant hub of craftsmanship, design, and inspiration.
picks.source: I amsterdam · Your Little Black Book

picks.title: Amsterdam Art Week
picks.venue: Rijksakademie van beeldende kunsten (national academy of fin
picks.blurb: Discover the contemporary art world Amsterdam Art Week invites you to explore the world of contemporary art. The city opens its doors to both established names and new talent.
picks.source: I amsterdam · Your Little Black Book

picks.title: De Pure Markt gaat naar binnen!
picks.blurb: 90+ independent makers and food vendors at the indoor market. Food, drinks, and curated goods.
picks.source: I amsterdam · Your Little Black Book

picks.title: IDFA: International Documentary Film Festival Amsterdam
picks.blurb: Largest documentary festival No other film festival in the world attracts as many high-quality documentaries, film fans, and film professionals from the Netherlands and abroad as IDFA.
picks.source: I amsterdam · Your Little Black Book · Het Parool PS

picks.title: Ligconcert® presents: lying down concert at the Maritime Museum
picks.blurb: 10,000 sparkling lights The one and only Ligconcert® at the Maritime Museum Amsterdam under the enchanting glass roof, illuminated by no fewer than 10,000 sparkling lights, is a magical experience.
picks.source: I amsterdam · Your Little Black Book

picks.title: noordermarkt
picks.blurb: Every Saturday, this is the place for your organic groceries, and on Mondays, you can shop for vintage, curiosities, and antiques.
picks.source: Your Little Black Book · I amsterdam

picks.title: Chez Matisse
picks.blurb: Vibrant Matisse works including rarely-loaned La Blouse roumaine; explores his influence on Rothko, Picasso, and modern art.
picks.why: Rare masterpiece and his lasting artistic influence
picks.source: I amsterdam · Your Little Black Book

picks.title: Yayoi Kusama
picks.venue: Stedelijk Museum - Modern and Contemporary Art and Design
picks.blurb: 70+ years of her career: paintings, sculptures, drawings, fashion, immersive installations with signature polka dots and mirrors.
picks.why: Iconic infinity rooms and mesmerizing installations
picks.source: I amsterdam · Your Little Black Book

picks.title: Le Foodwalk Winter
picks.blurb: Five-kilometre guided culinary walk through winter Amsterdam with stops at 5 restaurants (Vermeers Wijnkamer, In de Waag, Dignita Hoftuin, We Are EDN).
picks.source: I amsterdam · Your Little Black Book

picks.title: Willem de Kooning lezing
picks.blurb: 120 works tracing de Kooning's journey from Rotterdam to American modern art icon, emphasizing his drawings.
picks.why: First comprehensive Dutch overview of his drawings
picks.source: I amsterdam · Your Little Black Book

picks.title: Mire Lee: Vomit My Blessing
picks.blurb: Contemporary installation in historic church exploring identity, belief, and cultural intersection through provocative multimedia work.
picks.why: Bold contemporary art in sacred 14th-century space
picks.source: I amsterdam · Your Little Black Book

picks.title: Solo exhibition by Kaili Smith
picks.blurb: Australian-Dutch artist's first museum solo with paintings, films exploring youth culture, family, urban life, plus new commissioned work.
picks.source: I amsterdam · Your Little Black Book

picks.title: Cabaret – De musical met Chantal Janzen in de hoofdrol
picks.blurb: Chantal Janzen returns to musicals as Sally Bowles in a fresh Dutch production of the Berlin 1930s classic Cabaret.
picks.source: I amsterdam · Your Little Black Book

picks.title: Must see: major Yayoi Kusama exhibition at the Stedelijk
picks.blurb: You'll want to put this one on your list for the weekend (or one of the upcoming weekends): the major retrospective of Yayoi Kusama is currently on view at the…

picks.title: Bar François
picks.blurb: A new wine bar opened on Douwes Dekkerstraat this week. Bar François is the place to be for natural wine and small plates, and it has a very cozy atmosphere.

picks.title: Dinamo Pizza
picks.blurb: For a good New York-style pizza slice, you can now also head to the Elandsgracht. At Dinamo Pizza, they bake pizzas measuring a whopping 50 centimeters, which…

picks.title: Sea Palace Café
picks.blurb: New to the iconic Sea Palace on the Oosterdok: Sea Palace Café, a café and Chinese bakery run by the third generation of the But family.

picks.title: The Jollof Club
picks.blurb: Great news for lovers of West African cuisine! The Jollof Club is finally getting a permanent location in Amsterdam.

picks.title: Vermut in Oud-West
picks.blurb: The Jan Pieter Heijestraat has gained another great spot. At Vermut, you can enjoy sitting on the terrace or inside the warm interior.

picks.title: Vin Fou in Oud-West
picks.blurb: New on Jan Pieter Heijestraat: Vin Fou , the new French restaurant and bistro by Angelo Kremmydas, whom you also know from Gitane and Massalia.

picks.title: gastropub 't Lemmeke
picks.blurb: Amsterdam has a new favorite. Behind 't Lemmeke is the same team as behind Wijmpje Beukers, Schotsheuvel, and De Zingende Zwaan, but this time it is all about…

picks.title: KISEKI Sake Bar & Food
picks.blurb: New in the Helmersbuurt: KISEKI Sake Bar & Food, a cozy Japanese sake bar where you can also enjoy a great meal.

picks.title: new food hall Kade Noord
picks.blurb: There is a new hospitality spot by the water in Amsterdam North! Kade Noord is a new venue spanning a whopping 1.000 m².

picks.title: CABINET festive edition
picks.venue: Centrale Markthal, Jan van Galenstraat 4, Amsterdam-West <st
picks.blurb: After the October edition, CABINET returns to the Centrale Markthal in December for a special festive edition.

picks.title: Polish apple pie at Krush
picks.blurb: A new tip for everyone who loves apple pie! At Krush on Jacob van Lennepstraat, it's all about szarlotka, the Polish version of apple pie.

picks.title: Javaplein Vintage Market
picks.blurb: A Vintage Market is scheduled to take place on Javaplein again in December. It is a market where you can browse through second-hand clothing, vintage finds…

picks.title: Outdoor Market NoordOogst
picks.blurb: An outdoor market is held on the green grounds of NoordOogst every first Saturday of the month.

picks.title: Cinair Europe Drive-In Cinema
picks.blurb: Watch films from your car with sound via radio; bring snacks and friends for a unique drive-in movie night experience.
picks.why: Novel twist on cinema—watch from your vehicle

picks.title: Afternoon Tea at Mandarin Oriental Conservatory
picks.blurb: In the mood to catch up properly over Afternoon Tea? At Mandarin Oriental Conservatorium, Amsterdam, you can join us for Notes of Summer from Thursday through…

picks.title: Bistro de Fles on the Prinsengracht
picks.blurb: New on the Prinsengracht: Bistro de Fles, an atmospheric bistro in the basement with a dark, warm interior and a strong focus on wine and good food.

picks.title: Café Pietertje opens in Westerpark
picks.venue: Café Pietertje, Van Limburg Stirumplein 4-6, Amsterdam-West
picks.blurb: A new café is opening in the Staatsliedenbuurt! Next to Piet de Gruyter, there is now Café Pietertje on Van Limburg Stirumplein.

picks.title: Christian Tschida and Pieksman at Neighborhood Café De Tros
picks.blurb: A special Sunday for wine lovers at Buurtcafé De Tros! On November 22, Austrian winemaker Christian Tschida will be a guest, together with Pieksman.

picks.title: SPIN. Listening Bar & Pool Café in Oud-West
picks.blurb: New to the spot where Panache used to be on Ten Katestraat is SPIN., a hi-fi listening bar and pool café where music, food, cocktails, and pool come together.

picks.title: The ice rink on Museumplein is open again.
picks.blurb: The winter season in Amsterdam has officially begun, as the ice rink on Museumplein is open again!

picks.title: The Salon of the team behind De Tros
picks.blurb: A new restaurant to add to your list! You can now find De Salon on Witte de Withstraat, the new establishment from the team behind Buurtcafé De Tros.

picks.title: Wils Café opens on the Weesperzijde
picks.blurb: A new address to add to your list! Wils Café is now open on Weesperzijde. Chef Joris Bijdendijk's new establishment has the character of a French bistro, but…

picks.title: Amsterdam Museum Festival – 100 Years
picks.blurb: Century celebration with daily workshops, tours, exhibitions; kids can hunt clues discovering Amsterdam through missions.

picks.title: Oorkaan Ensemble - Vijf! (5+)
picks.blurb: Four musicians perform a musical celebration blending Turkish sounds with contemporary beats for families.
picks.why: Family-friendly musical performance with international flair

picks.title: grammes
picks.blurb: This bakery, which has made its home on the Maasstraat, says goodbye this weekend. An institution for those in Zuid, grammes was one of the many spots that…

picks.title: Swan Lake
picks.blurb: Unfortunately, the performances in October 2026 and November 2026 are sold out. This show will return in April 2027.
picks.source: I amsterdam · Your Little Black Book

picks.title: Exhibition: the ESSENCE
picks.venue: STRAAT Museum – Street art en graffiti in Amsterdam
picks.blurb: Core elements of graffiti The exhibition focuses on the core elements of graffiti: names, tags, lines and repetition as the building blocks of a visual system.

picks.title: Science & Cocktails: Fungal networks and the wave nature of life
picks.blurb: How do mycelial networks of a fungus - a brainless organism - manage to exhibit apparently sentient behaviors?

picks.title: Fonduytje
picks.blurb: You probably know IJscuypje for its ice cream, but this autumn you’ll be introduced to the wintry edition: Fonduytje.

picks.title: Cobra Museum
picks.blurb: Art that challenges, surprises and inspires wonder: this weekend, Museum Cobra opens 2 new exhibitions in which nothing is ordinary.

picks.title: Humans of Film Festival
picks.blurb: At Humans of Film Festival, you’ll discover extraordinary stories from every corner of the world.

picks.title: Where the Light Comes In – Days of Izyum
picks.blurb: What does everyday life look like in a place where nothing can be taken for granted? In Where the Light Comes In – Days of Izyum , artist and filmmaker Kiki Ho…

picks.title: Hailun Ma: Hometown
picks.blurb: Her first major solo show outside China — fashion as a lens on Xinjiang, its people and its landscapes, one of the three exhibitions Foam reopened with.
picks.why: Foam is back · the show to see

picks.title: STRAAT Collectie
picks.venue: STRAAT Museum – Street art en graffiti in Amsterdam
picks.blurb: Museum for street art and graffiti We focus on curating a collection that truly reflects the international street art movement.

picks.title: Kaboom X Melkweg Cinema
picks.blurb: Anime in the Milky Way Kaboom regularly organizes an anime night at the Melkweg Cinema, so you can once again enjoy the best anime on the big screen!

picks.title: Queer Amsterdam, the Pink City
picks.blurb: Discover the history You will discover the eventful history of the Amsterdam LGBTQIA+ community. This exhibition offers you a cultural-historical story.

picks.title: De Roode Remise Singing Session
picks.blurb: De Roode Remise Singing Session The core singers know each other from the famous Backroom Sessions at Mulligan's Irish Bar, but everyone, experienced or inexperienced, is welcome, as is every genre.

picks.title: Exhibition Worn in the Rijksmuseum
picks.blurb: WORN shows how clothing can lead a life of its own In this presentation, you discover worn, repaired and altered pieces from the collection, dating from 1640 to 1930.

picks.title: Humans And Friends presents Music Quest: A Live Role-Playing Musical Game
picks.blurb: Let's plug and play We're inviting you to join us on a very special Music Quest, a live role-playing musical game!

picks.title: SCIM Amsterdam 2026 – Settimana della Cucina Italiana nel Mondo
picks.blurb: Italian cuisine festival: masterclasses, live cooking, competition, B2B meetings celebrating Italian food culture and UNESCO heritage.

picks.title: Sint op Solder
picks.blurb: Explore the secrets of Sinterklaas in this atmospheric historic house with a hidden church in the attic.
picks.why: Festive seasonal immersion in unique historic setting

picks.title: Groove Beest Familieconcert: Kay Slice
picks.blurb: Hiphop and afrobeat meet ancient sounds and storytelling in this family-friendly concert.
picks.why: Contemporary world music fusion introducing kids to global r

picks.title: What is Film?
picks.blurb: Various moving image components are highlighted on the ground floor and throughout the building. Browse through Eye's unique collection or make your own flip book or animated film.

picks.title: Ulrich Seidl – Über das Leben, die Liebe und den Tod
picks.blurb: Featuring a wealth of early, little-known and newly commissioned (film) works by the Austrian filmmaker, photographer and theatre-maker, the exhibition confronts visitors with the lives of a number of…
picks.imageCredit: still Im Keller (Ulrich Seidl, AT 2014) © Ulrich Seidl Filmproduktion

picks.title: Everyday Blues – The Films of Charles Burnett
picks.when: Opens Thu 26 Nov · until Wed 23 Dec
picks.blurb: The seldom-screened films of legendary American filmmaker Charles Burnett, a pioneer of the Black independent cinema movement of the ’70s and ’80s known as L.A. Rebellion.

picks.title: Pure Markt
picks.blurb: An artisan food-and-craft market in a green park — small makers, slow food and a relaxed Sunday-stroll crowd in Frankendael.
picks.source: Your Little Black Book · Pure Markt · Maps

picks.title: IJ-Hallen
picks.blurb: Europe’s biggest flea market — 750 stalls across two NDSM shipyard warehouses, a proper treasure-hunt of vintage and junk.

picks.title: ARTIS-Aquarium
picks.blurb: The 1882 aquarium building, newly restored: glowing tanks, coral rooms and an underwater Amsterdam canal — the rainy-day ace of the Plantage.
picks.source: Ness canon · Your Little Black Book

picks.title: Pllek — waterfront hang
picks.blurb: A cargo-container café-bar on the NDSM wharf — big windows onto the IJ, sofas, and a wood stove when it turns.
picks.why: Indoor seating · IJ views · cozy when grey

picks.title: Café Chris — oldest brown café
picks.blurb: Open since 1624: a creaky, golden-lit Jordaan brown café for a slow afternoon beer while it pours outside.

picks.title: Foodhallen
picks.blurb: An indoor food hall in a converted tram depot — 20-odd stalls, long tables and two bars under one roof.
picks.why: Indoor · grazing for a crowd · weather-proof

picks.title: Bloemenmarkt
picks.blurb: The world’s only floating flower market — barges of tulips, bulbs and seeds moored along the Singel since 1862.

picks.title: Sauna Deco — Art Deco baths
picks.blurb: A 1920s Art Deco bathhouse (salvaged from a Paris department store) with saunas, steam and a quiet tea room.
picks.why: Warm · restorative · the ultimate cold-and-wet antidote

picks.title: Vondelpark playgrounds
picks.blurb: Amsterdam’s favourite park: open-air playgrounds, the Kinderkookkafé, ducks and room to run.
picks.why: Free · easy any time with kids

picks.title: Vermut
picks.blurb: A dedicated vermouth-and-aperitivo bar on the JP Heijestraat — Spanish-style early evenings, no reservations culture required.
picks.why: Aperitivo hour finally gets a home

picks.title: Marocaine
picks.blurb: Chef Rachid El Mouhandiz, who scored a 9- in Het Parool, turns his Jordaan spot into a full ode to Moroccan cooking.

picks.title: Zuiver Wijnen
picks.blurb: Natural wine bar and bottle shop on the IJ-side quay behind Central — low-intervention bottles without the ceremony.

picks.title: MAZE Festival 2026: Book of Returns
picks.blurb: Featured this week by Subbacultcha.

picks.title: The Movies — arthouse cinema
picks.blurb: The Netherlands’ oldest cinema still running — Art Deco rooms, a dinner-and-a-film deal, arthouse bills.
picks.why: Indoor · dinner + a film · perfect when it’s wet

picks.title: Two Story
picks.venue: Two Story — gallery, design store & café
picks.blurb: An 18th-century canal house rebuilt by Copenhagen's Atelier Axo: design store up front, courtyard café, gallery rotating every three months.
picks.why: Copenhagen design eye, Amsterdam canal house

picks.title: East Beach — rooftop city beach
picks.blurb: A new 800m² rooftop city beach above Oosterpark — sand, beach chairs, drinks, open to all.

picks.title: Foam
picks.blurb: A nimble photography museum in a canal house — big-name retrospectives and emerging talent, always worth the drop-in.

picks.title: Droog
picks.blurb: Where Dutch conceptual design was born: gallery, shop, courtyard garden and a single hotel room in a Staalstraat warehouse.

picks.title: MENDO
picks.blurb: A self-described candy store for book aficionados: black-walled cabinet of photography, design and fashion monographs.

picks.title: Moise
picks.blurb: An understated De Pijp boutique with a razor-sharp eye — Acne, Lemaire, Marant and the like, hand-picked and beautifully shown.

picks.title: Patta
picks.blurb: The homegrown streetwear label and culture hub — drops, sneakers and the community that put Amsterdam on the map.

picks.title: X Bank
picks.blurb: A concept store in a former bank showing 180+ Dutch fashion, design and art labels — couture to hand-thrown ceramics.
picks.why: Best of Dutch design · one room

picks.title: Melkweg
picks.blurb: A former dairy turned multi-room culture machine — live music, club nights, film and a gallery, all under one roof.

picks.title: Mobilia
picks.blurb: Three floors of high design on the Utrechtsestraat — icons by the masters alongside more attainable covetables.

picks.title: Utrecht
picks.blurb: Amsterdam’s quieter little sister — wharf-side canals, the soaring Dom Tower and a real café culture, minus the crowds.

picks.title: Vlieger
picks.blurb: A two-floor temple to paper since 1869 — hundreds of colours, handmade sheets and card stacked to the ceiling.

picks.title: Efteling
picks.blurb: Europe’s oldest fairytale theme park — enchanted forest, dark rides and proper coasters in a storybook world.

picks.title: Micropia
picks.blurb: The world’s only microbe museum — microscopes, a kiss-o-meter and the tiny life all around us.

picks.title: Kriterion
picks.blurb: A legendary student-run cinema and café since 1945 — arthouse programming with a buzzy terrace.

picks.title: Madurodam
picks.blurb: The whole of the Netherlands at 1:25 — miniature canals, Schiphol and windmills kids can tower over.

picks.title: Nxt Museum
picks.blurb: Warehouse-scale new-media museum in Noord: room-sized audiovisual installations rewired each season by artists and coders.

picks.title: Muiderslot
picks.blurb: A moated medieval castle on the IJmeer — turrets, falconry and a walled garden, the best-preserved fortress in the country.

picks.title: Dappermarkt
picks.blurb: A buzzing, multicultural Oost street market — spices, textiles and world food at honest neighbourhood prices.

picks.title: Rijksmuseum
picks.blurb: The Netherlands’ treasure house — Rembrandt’s Night Watch, Vermeer and the Golden Age masters in a cathedral of a building.
picks.why: The Night Watch · the big one

picks.title: De Filmhallen
picks.blurb: A nine-screen arthouse cinema in a converted tram depot — with a bustling food hall right next door.
picks.why: Arthouse · in the old tram depot

picks.title: Eye Filmmuseum — repertory screening
picks.blurb: Across the IJ by free ferry: a striking film museum with a daily repertory programme and a river-view café.
picks.why: Indoor · a film + the ferry ride · weather-proof

picks.title: Huis Marseille
picks.blurb: The city’s first photography museum, across two canal houses with a hidden garden — beautifully curated, never crowded.

picks.title: Museum Van Loon
picks.blurb: A patrician canal house still furnished as lived: portraits, coach house, and the quietest formal garden inside the ring.

picks.title: Marken & Volendam
picks.blurb: Two former Zuiderzee fishing villages — wooden houses, working harbours and smoked eel, an easy half-day from Centraal.

picks.title: Zandvoort Beach
picks.blurb: The nearest North Sea beach — wide sands, beach clubs and a direct train from Centraal; in summer half the city decamps here.

picks.title: Albert Cuypmarkt
picks.blurb: The Netherlands’ biggest street market — 250-odd stalls of stroopwafels, cheese, fabric and flowers the length of De Pijp.

picks.title: Kinderdijk Windmills
picks.blurb: Nineteen 18th-century windmills lined along the polders — the postcard Dutch landscape, a UNESCO site you can walk or cycle.

picks.title: Waterlooplein Flea Market
picks.blurb: The city’s oldest flea market — secondhand everything, vintage denim, records and bric-a-brac spread out beside the Stopera.
